_meta.note: Write the Tier-1 + Tier-2 missing how-tos, dogfooded. Each mechanism guide ships a runnable, self-verifying proof under docs/howto/gate-examples/ (deterministic, marker-emitting) bundled into a new node-suite group T77; the two prose guides are integrity-checked by prose-check.sh and folded into T62. The parallel and fully-local guides are additionally validated by a real Ollama run (non-gating live tier, like tests/real-backend.sh). Spec-first: each phase's first task authors the proof/contract before the guide. Flips 6 roadmap gaps from Not-available to created in howto-list.md + docs/howto/README.md.

phases.title: Run tasks in parallel (+ worktree isolation)

tasks.title: Author the parallel-fanout proof
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/parallel-fanout.sh — a self-contained deterministic proof (own tiny stub backend, git-enabled temp project) that (a) hb ready returns the independent runnable set and excludes a requires-dependent task, (b) a worktree-isolated concurrent fan-out (HB_MAX_CONCURRENCY>1) runs two independent tasks writing DISTINCT files and merges both into the main tree, (c) worktrees/temp branches are cleaned up after. Prints PARALLEL-FANOUT-OK only when all hold. Deterministic (stub worker, no model).

tasks.title: Write the guide + wire it
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/run-tasks-in-parallel.md (hb ready N, exec run --parallel N, HB_MAX_CONCURRENCY, worktree isolation, the same-files conflict rule, when to fan out). Add node-suite group T77 to tests/run-tests.sh running docs/howto/gate-examples/parallel-fanout.sh (marker) + prose-check on the guide. Flip the roadmap rows in docs/howto/howto-list.md (Run Independent Tasks in Parallel; Understand Worktree Isolation) and add an index row in docs/howto/README.md. Validate live: a real Ollama-backed parallel run (recorded, non-gating).

phases.title: Add HeartBeat to an existing repository

tasks.title: Author the existing-repo proof
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/existing-repo.sh — a deterministic proof that in a pre-existing git repo (an existing tracked file + commit), hb init / bootstrap adds .hb WITHOUT clobbering existing files or history: the existing file's contents are unchanged, the pre-existing commit still reachable, and a subsequent gate pass (committed with git --no-verify so the rot hook can't flake the assertion) records new work without altering the pre-existing file. Prints EXISTING-REPO-OK only when all hold.

tasks.title: Write the guide + wire it
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/add-heartbeat-to-an-existing-repo.md (hb init into a live repo, what .hb adds, .gitignore guidance, HB_NO_GIT / HB_GIT_AUTOCOMMIT for existing CI, coexistence with existing history). Add the existing-repo.sh proof + prose-check on the guide to node-suite group T77. Flip the howto-list.md row (Add HeartBeat to an Existing Repository) and add a docs/howto/README.md index row.

tasks.title: Author the sparse-deps proof
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/sparse-deps.sh — a deterministic proof over two lint-clean DAGs with the same three tasks: an OVER-CONSTRAINED one (A->B->C serial requires) where hb ready returns exactly 1, and a SPARSE one (only real deps) where hb ready returns 3 — showing over-constraint needlessly serializes work. Prints SPARSE-DEPS-OK only when both ready-set sizes match.

tasks.title: Write the guide + wire it
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/write-sparse-dependencies.md (requires models REAL data/order deps only; over-constraint kills parallelism; how to spot it via the hb ready set size; the same-files caveat that argues for a real edge). Add sparse-deps.sh + prose-check to node-suite group T77. Flip the howto-list.md row (Write Dependencies That Don't Over-Constrain) and add a docs/howto/README.md index row.

tasks.title: Author the unsafe-gate proof
tasks.description: Spec-first: write docs/howto/gate-examples/unsafe-gate.sh — a deterministic proof that hb audit FLAGS the risky gate patterns a reviewer must catch: a side_effecting gate (writes/creates files, can fabricate its own evidence) and a nondeterministic gate (network/time), while a clean behavioral gate audits with no such finding. Prints UNSAFE-GATE-OK only when the auditor reports side_effecting AND nondeterministic on the bad DAG and neither on the good one.

tasks.title: Write the guide + wire it
tasks.description: Write docs/howto/review-an-unsafe-gate.md (gate cmds are arbitrary shell run with your privileges; what to look for; how hb audit flags side_effecting / nondeterministic; observe-don't-produce; run untrusted DAGs with least privilege). Link the auditor guide rather than restating its rules. Add unsafe-gate.sh + prose-check to node-suite group T77. Flip the howto-list.md row (A Gate Command Looks Unsafe) and add a docs/howto/README.md index row.

tasks.title: Draft the fully-local guide contract
tasks.description: Author docs/howto/run-heartbeat-fully-locally.md: the end-to-end no-cloud story — pip install the Python port, the ollama backend (no API key, stdlib only), Python gates, no node, no Claude Code. Real hb commands only (hb init / audit / exec / gate); link use-heartbeat-with-ollama.md and choose-runtime.md rather than duplicating them; substantive (>=15 non-blank lines), no placeholders — must pass prose-check.sh.

tasks.title: Wire + live-validate
tasks.description: Add docs/howto/run-heartbeat-fully-locally.md to the T62 prose bundle in tests/run-tests.sh (bump the ALL-PROSE-OK count). Flip the howto-list.md rows (Run HeartBeat Fully Locally; Run HeartBeat Without Claude Code) and add a docs/howto/README.md index row. Validate live: a real Ollama-backed end-to-end run via py/real-backend.py (recorded, non-gating).

tasks.title: Draft the scheduling guide contract
tasks.description: Author docs/howto/schedule-heartbeat-unattended.md: driving ticks unattended — the /schedule cron routine (Claude Code, cloud caveat: clones a git repo), system cron calling headless claude -p or hb tick for local-only projects, and /loop for in-session. Real hb commands only (hb tick); link the SKILL/relevant guides; substantive, no placeholders — must pass prose-check.sh.

tasks.title: Wire it
tasks.description: Add docs/howto/schedule-heartbeat-unattended.md to the T62 prose bundle in tests/run-tests.sh (bump the ALL-PROSE-OK count). Flip the howto-list.md row (Schedule HeartBeat with Cron) and add a docs/howto/README.md index row.

GATE_PAR.desc: The parallel/worktree guide ships a real, deterministic proof (fan-out isolates + merges + cleans up), passes prose-integrity, and is wired into the suite.

review.prompt: Refute that PAR is done: does parallel-fanout.sh actually run tasks CONCURRENTLY in ISOLATED worktrees and assert BOTH distinct files merged, or could PARALLEL-FANOUT-OK print on a trivial serial run? does it prove hb ready excludes a requires-dependent task? are worktrees really cleaned up? does the guide claim behavior the proof doesn't show? is the marker printed unconditionally?

criteria.desc: the parallel fan-out proof passes (isolate + merge + cleanup)
the guide passes prose-integrity (links + real commands)
the suite actually runs the proof AND asserts its marker (not mere file existence)

GATE_REPO.desc: The existing-repo guide ships a deterministic proof that hb init is non-destructive in a live repo, passes prose-integrity, and is wired.

review.prompt: Refute that REPO is done: does existing-repo.sh actually start from a repo with a pre-existing tracked file AND commit, and assert the file is byte-unchanged and the old commit still reachable after hb init? or could EXISTING-REPO-OK print without any pre-existing content to clobber? does the guide over-promise?

criteria.desc: the existing-repo proof passes (init is non-destructive)
the suite actually runs the proof AND asserts its marker

GATE_DEPS.desc: The sparse-deps guide ships a deterministic proof that over-constraint serializes the ready set, passes prose-integrity, and is wired.

review.prompt: Refute that DEPS is done: does sparse-deps.sh really compare ready-set sizes for an over-constrained vs a sparse DAG (1 vs 3), or does it assert something trivial? are both DAGs lint-clean (so the difference is the requires edges, not a structural error)? could SPARSE-DEPS-OK print if hb ready returned the same for both?

criteria.desc: the suite actually runs the proof AND asserts its marker

GATE_SAFE.desc: The unsafe-gate guide ships a deterministic proof that the auditor flags side_effecting + nondeterministic gates, passes prose-integrity, and is wired.

review.prompt: Refute that SAFE is done: does unsafe-gate.sh assert the auditor reports BOTH side_effecting AND nondeterministic on the bad DAG AND neither on the good one, or does it accept a partial/empty result? could UNSAFE-GATE-OK print if audit found nothing? does the guide restate the auditor rules (drift risk) instead of linking them?

criteria.desc: the unsafe-gate proof passes (auditor flags side_effecting + nondeterministic)
the suite actually runs the proof AND asserts its marker

GATE_LOCAL.desc: The fully-local guide passes prose-integrity and is folded into the T62 prose bundle.

criteria.desc: the guide passes prose-integrity (links + real commands)
the guide is wired into a real prose-check invocation (T62 bundle), not just mentioned
